translation_en: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Jarir. And Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us. And Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan. All of them reported from al-A‘mash with this chain, with a similar report.

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet was asked about marrying Hamzah’s daughter. He said, “She is not lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding, and what is forbidden through blood relationship is forbidden through breastfeeding.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Mihran al-Quta‘i narrated to us: Bishr ibn Umar narrated to us. Both reported from Shu‘bah. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn Abi Arubah. Both reported from Qatadah with Hammam’s chain, with the same meaning. However, Shu‘bah’s report ends at the words, “the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding.” Sa‘id’s report says, “What is forbidden through breastfeeding is forbidden through lineage.” In Bishr ibn Umar’s report is the wording, “I heard Jabir ibn Zayd.”

Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli and Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Makhramah ibn Bukayr informed me, from his father, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Muslim say: I heard Muhammad ibn Muslim say: I heard Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman say: I heard Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, say: The Messenger of Allah was asked, “Messenger of Allah, what about Hamzah’s daughter? Will you not marry the daughter of Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib?” He said, “Hamzah is my brother through breastfeeding.”

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Ala, narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Hisham informed us: My father informed us, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, who said: The Messenger of Allah came to me, and I said, “Would you consider marrying my sister, the daughter of Abu Sufyan?” He said, “What would I do?” I said, “Marry her.” He said, “Would you like that?” I said, “I am not the only wife you have, and the person I would most like to share in good with me is my sister.” He said, “She is not lawful for me.” I said, “I was told that you are proposing to Durrah bint Abi Salamah.” He said, “The daughter of Umm Salamah?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Even if she were not my stepdaughter in my care, she would not be lawful for me, for she is the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding. Thuwaybah breastfed me and her father Abu Salamah. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters.”

Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated to me: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us. Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: al-Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us: Zuhayr informed us. Both reported from Hisham ibn Urwah with this chain, with the same wording.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, who narrated to him that Zaynab bint Abi Salamah narrated to him that Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, told her: She said to the Messenger of Allah, “Messenger of Allah, marry my sister Azza.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Would you like that?” She said, “Yes, Messenger of Allah. I am not the only wife you have, and the person I would most like to share in good with me is my sister.” The Messenger of Allah said, “That is not lawful for me.” She said, “Messenger of Allah, we have heard that you intend to marry Durrah bint Abi Salamah.” He said, “The daughter of Abu Salamah?” She said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Even if she were not my stepdaughter in my care, she would not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through breastfeeding: Thuwaybah breastfed me and Abu Salamah. So do not offer me your daughters or your sisters.”

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu‘ayb ibn al-Layth narrated this to me: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, who narrated to me: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me. Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim al-Zuhri informed me: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim narrated to us. Both reported from al-Zuhri with Ibn Abi Habib’s chain, a report similar to his. None of them named Azza in his report except Yazid ibn Abi Habib.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Ismail narrated to us. Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us. Both reported from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said—and Suwayd and Zuhayr said, “The Prophet said”—“One or two sucklings do not establish the prohibition of marriage through breastfeeding.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Amr al-Naqid, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, all reporting from al-Mu‘tamir; this is Yahya’s wording. Al-Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman informed us, from Ayyub, who reported from Abu al-Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet of Allah while he was in my house and said, “Prophet of Allah, I had a wife, then married another. My first wife claims that she breastfed my new wife once or twice.” The Prophet of Allah said, “One or two instances of suckling do not establish the prohibition.” Amr’s report says: from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal.

Abu Ghassan al-Misma‘i narrated to me: Muadh narrated to us. Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muadh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Salih ibn Abi Maryam, Abu al-Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, that a man from Banu Amir ibn Sa‘sa‘ah said, “Prophet of Allah, does one suckling make marriage forbidden?” He said, “No.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, that Umm al-Fadl narrated that the Prophet of Allah said, “One or two sucklings, or one or two instances of suckling, do not make marriage forbidden.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated this to us, both from Abdah ibn Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Arubah, with this chain. Ishaq said, as in Ibn Bishr’s report, “or two sucklings, or two instances of suckling.” Ibn Abi Shaybah said, “and two sucklings and two instances of suckling.”

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from Umm al-Fadl, from the Prophet, who said, “One or two instances of suckling do not establish the prohibition.”

Ahmad ibn Sa‘id al-Darimi narrated to me: Habban narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, that a man asked the Prophet, “Does one instance of suckling make marriage forbidden?” He said, “No.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Amrah, from Aishah, who said: Among what was revealed in the Quran was that ten known sucklings made marriage forbidden. Then they were abrogated by five known sucklings. The Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was recited from the Quran.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah al-Qa‘nabi narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Yahya, Ibn Sa‘id, from Amrah, who heard Aishah say—while discussing what makes marriage forbidden through breastfeeding—Amrah said that Aishah stated: “Ten known sucklings were revealed in the Quran; then five known sucklings were also revealed.”
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say: Amrah informed me that she heard Aishah say the same.

Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Aishah, who said: Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Prophet and said, “Messenger of Allah, I see displeasure on Abu Hudhayfah’s face because Salim, his ally, comes into our home.” The Prophet said, “Breastfeed him.” She said, “How can I breastfeed him when he is a grown man?” The Messenger of Allah smiled and said, “I know that he is a grown man.” Amr added in his report: He had been present at Badr. In Ibn Abi Umar’s version, the Messenger of Allah laughed.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Muhammad ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, both from al-Thaqafi. Ibn Abi Umar said: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Qasim, from Aishah, that Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, lived with Abu Hudhayfah and his family in their home. Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Prophet and said, “Salim has reached the age men reach and understands what men understand. He comes to us, and I think Abu Hudhayfah feels discomfort about that.” The Prophet said to her, “Breastfeed him and you will become forbidden to him, and what Abu Hudhayfah feels will go away.” She returned and said, “I breastfed him, and what Abu Hudhayfah felt has gone away.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us; these are Ibn Rafi’s words. He said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed us that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr informed him that Aishah informed him that Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn Amr came to the Prophet and said, “Messenger of Allah, Salim—the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah—is with us in our home. He has reached the age men reach and understands what men understand.” He said, “Breastfeed him, and you will become forbidden to him.” I refrained from relating it for a year or nearly a year, and I was apprehensive about it. Then I met al-Qasim and said, “You told me a hadith that I have not related since.” He asked, “What is it?” I told him. He said, “Relate it on my authority: Aishah informed me of it.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Nafi, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, who said: Umm Salamah said to Aishah, “A young man, who has not reached maturity, comes in to you, but I would not like him to come in to me.” Aishah said, “Do you not have an example in the Messenger of Allah?” She said, “The wife of Abu Hudhayfah said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Salim comes in to me while he is a man, and Abu Hudhayfah feels discomfort about him.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Breastfeed him so that he may come in to you.’”

Abu al-Tahir and Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli narrated this to me; these are Harun’s words. They said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Makhramah ibn Bukayr informed me, from his father, who said: I heard Humayd ibn Nafi say: I heard Zaynab bint Abi Salamah say: I heard Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, say to Aishah, “By Allah, I do not feel comfortable with a boy seeing me after he has no further need for breastfeeding.” She said, “Why? Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Messenger of Allah and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I see displeasure on Abu Hudhayfah’s face because Salim comes in.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Breastfeed him.’ She said, ‘He has a beard.’ He said, ‘Breastfeed him, and what is on Abu Hudhayfah’s face will go away.’” She said, “By Allah, I did not recognize anything on Abu Hudhayfah’s face.”

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu‘ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, who narrated to me: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Zam‘ah informed me that his mother, Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, informed him that her mother, Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, used to say: The other wives of the Prophet refused to allow anyone to enter upon them through this kind of breastfeeding. They said to Aishah, “By Allah, we consider this only a concession that the Messenger of Allah granted specifically to Salim. No one will enter upon us through this kind of breastfeeding, nor will we see it as applicable.”

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Ash‘ath ibn Abi al-Sha‘tha, from his father, from Masruq, who said: Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah came in to me while a man was sitting with me. This displeased him greatly, and I saw anger on his face. I said, “Messenger of Allah, he is my brother through breastfeeding.” She said that he replied, “Consider carefully who your brothers through breastfeeding are, for breastfeeding that establishes kinship is that which satisfies hunger.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated this to us: They said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us. Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us: My father narrated to us. All of them narrated to us from Shu‘bah. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us. Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us. All of them reported from Sufyan. Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Husayn al-Ju‘fi narrated to us, from Za’idah. All of them reported from Ash‘ath ibn Abi al-Sha‘tha with Abu al-Ahwas’s chain and a similar meaning, except that they said, “that which satisfies hunger.”

Ubaydullah ibn Umar ibn Maysarah al-Qawariri narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salih, Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Alqamah al-Hashimi, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that on the day of Hunayn the Messenger of Allah sent an army to Awtas. They met an enemy, fought them, and overcame them, taking captive women. Some of the Messenger of Allah’s companions felt uneasy about having relations with them because their husbands were polytheists. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning this: “And married women are forbidden to you, except those whom your right hands possess” Quran 4:24, meaning that they are lawful for you once their waiting period has ended.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: They said: Abd al-A‘la narrated to us, from Sa‘id, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, that Abu Alqamah al-Hashimi narrated that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri narrated to them that the Prophet of Allah sent out a detachment on the day of Hunayn. This is similar to the hadith of Yazid ibn Zuray, except that he said, “Except those whom your right hands possess among them are lawful for you,” and he did not mention “once their waiting period has ended.”
Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated this to me: Khalid—Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, with this chain, similarly.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated this to me: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Sa‘id, who said: They took captive women at Awtas who had husbands, and they were apprehensive, so this verse was revealed: “And married women are forbidden to you, except those whom your right hands possess” Quran 4:24.
